speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Bartholomew's boy came by the shop door. They go into the barley at Hewlands at six tomorrow.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: At six. Then they are cutting before the dew is off the headland.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The ear is short. If he waits on the sun it will shed in the stubble. He sent word when the sickles start. He did not send a cart.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: He is asking whether thy feet can get as far as Shottery.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fetch the old country shoes. We shall see what two pair of worsted hose will do.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: If thou weepest when the heel goes in, I am telling the twins.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: In, and laced, and nobody weeping. They will come off again until morning.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Standing on a rush mat is not ten hours in barley stubble.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I bound behind his sickles before you were tall enough to twist a band. The hands remember the twist.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The hands have held a quill since April. Take a leather thumb-stall from the shop, or you will have thistles in every finger before noon.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: There are two paring-guards on the peg. Take the wide one.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six in the morning till four in the afternoon, with an hour for bread when he calls it.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: And home before the evening. Master Quiney and Master Sturley sit down at half past six. I will not have you at the board smelling of the ditch.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Let him smell of barley. Since they come to talk of malt, it will save them bringing a bushel in at the door.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Take the shoes off until morning. There is no profit in wearing the skin thin in the hall.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Off they come. Set the small beer by the door tonight, and wake me before five.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: The house wakes before five every day. Thou art the only one who calls it an event.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: The lane to Shottery is dry. I will leave the shop latch on the pin.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: And leave the writing-case on the shelf. Two leaves of salt and rush-lights is enough ink for one Monday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bundle has not been untied since I came in. It can sleep another night.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Give me the shoes. Half the grease in this kitchen goes on the heels that walk up from London.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Grease the heel-seam, Joan, and no speech with the grease. Into the parlour, Will, and keep the foot up till supper.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The foot is up. Six is the hour, and the list is already dry.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Then six is the hour. The barley will not wait on a fair copy.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The fair copy is done. Tomorrow is a back, not a quill.
